sections.body:
A favourite food is the food you like most. It is the one you hope to see on the table. Every person has one, and every favourite is different.

A favourite food can be anything. It can be sweet, like ice cream or a mango. It can be salty, like fried chicken or a bowl of noodles. It can be plain, like rice with egg. It can even be a food other children do not like at all.

Why do we like some foods and not others? Taste is only one part of it. Food also has a smell, a texture, and a colour. A crunchy apple is different from a soft one. A hot bowl of soup on a cold day feels good in the stomach, not only on the tongue.

Memory matters too. Many people love a food because of a happy moment. A bowl of cháo reminds one child of their grandmother. Another child loves fruit because it was on a holiday trip.

There is nothing wrong with having a favourite food. But one food alone is not enough for a body. A plate with many kinds of food on it gives you everything you need.
examples: My favourite food is fried spring rolls.
I like this soup because it is hot and salty.
sections.heading: What is a favourite food?

sections.body:
Ask a hundred children, and you get a hundred answers. Here are some that many people love.

Phở is Vietnam's warm breakfast soup. It has rice noodles, meat and herbs on top. People eat it in the morning, and they eat it again at night.

Pizza comes from Italy, but the whole world eats it. It has bread dough, tomato sauce and cheese, and it is cut in triangles.

Sushi is Japanese. It is made of rice with fish on top, or with vegetables. You eat it with chopsticks, and you take one piece at a time.

Tacos are Mexican. A soft tortilla holds meat, beans, cheese and salad, and you fold it up to eat it.

Noodles are loved everywhere. In Vietnam we have bún, phở, mì and hủ tiếu. In Japan there is ramen. In China there are many kinds too.

Ice cream is a favourite for people of every age. It is cold and sweet, and it melts in your mouth.

Fruit is a favourite too, and a healthy one. Mangoes, bananas and apples are cheap and easy to find.

Notice how different they are. That is the good part. A world where everybody liked the same food would be a dull world to eat in.
examples: I love pizza on a Friday.
The favourite food of my friend is noodles.
sections.heading: Favourite foods around the world

sections.body:
Telling your family what you like is easy when you use the right words. Here is how.

First, think about it. Is there one food you always hope to see? Is it a taste, a smell, or a happy memory?

Next, say it clearly. Say the name of the food and say that you like it. Do not just say "it is fine".

Then say why. A reason helps the grown-ups understand. You can say the taste, the smell, the crunchiness, or the happy memory behind it.

After that, be **kind** about other people's food. Somebody at the table may not like the very thing you love, and that is alright too.

Last, be brave and try one thing. Take a small bite of a food you have never eaten. You do not have to finish it. One small bite is enough for today.
examples: I like it because it is crispy and warm.
I do not like olives, but I will try one.
sections.heading: How to say what you like
steps: Think about the food you like most.
Say the name of the food and say that you like it.
Be kind about what other people like.
Try one small bite of a new food.

sections.body:
These words help you talk about food with grown-ups and with other children.

Your **favourite** is the one you like most. Favourite comes from the word favour, which means the thing you wish for. You can say favourite about food, a colour, a song, or a friend.

To **dislike** something means that you do not like it. Nobody is wrong for disliking a food. Some people dislike the smell of fish, and some people dislike the texture of mushrooms.

To **try** a food means to taste it for the first time. Trying is a brave thing to do, and you are allowed to say no after one bite.

The **taste** of a food is what your tongue tells you. Sweet, sour, salty and bitter are the four main tastes. Some foods have more than one of them.

And a **kind** word is a polite word. When you do not like something, you can still be kind about it. "I do not like the smell of it" is kinder than "this is disgusting".
examples: I do not like mushrooms, but I will try some.
The taste is sweet and a little sour.
sections.heading: The words we use for our food

terms.example: My favourite food is spring rolls.

terms.example: The taste of this mango is very sweet.

terms.example: It is kind to say thank you for the food.

sections.body:
Trying a new food sounds hard, but it is really not. Here is a small way to do it.

Start with the smallest amount you can. One spoonful. One bite. Half a piece. Small is fine.

Look at it first. A new food is often a new colour, and colours are nice.

Smell it. Some food smells strong before it tastes good. That is normal.

Now take one bite and wait a moment. Your tongue needs a second to tell you what it thinks.

If you like it, have more. If you do not like it, that is alright too. Say thank you to the cook, and you have still been brave.

Many grown-ups have foods they did not like when they were seven and love now. Trying once is how they found out. Try one new food this week, and tell somebody how it went.
examples: The smell is strong, but I will try a bite.
I did not like it, and that is alright.
sections.heading: Trying one new food

sections.body:
Your favourite food is a wonderful thing. But your body needs more than one kind of food.

A good plate has a few parts. It has **rice or noodles**, which give you energy to run and to think. It has a **dish with protein**, like eggs, fish, chicken, tofu or beans, which helps you grow. It has **vegetables**, which give you vitamins and keep your tummy working. And it has **fruit**, which is sweet, full of water, and easy to share.

Think of the colours. If your plate is all white and brown, add something green, like rau muống or broccoli. If it has no red, add a tomato. Bright plates are not only pretty. Every colour brings something different.

Some days you will feel like only your favourite food. That happens. Then have it, and enjoy it. But try to add one more thing, even a small one.

And here is the good news. In Vietnam, a family meal already has this shape. Rice, a dish, a bowl of soup and a plate of vegetables. When you sit down at that table, you are already eating well.
examples: My plate has rice, soup, vegetables and fish.
I added some green vegetables to my plate.
A bright plate is a healthy plate.
sections.heading: A plate with many colours makes a good plate

item.summary: Everyone has a favourite food, and there is nothing wrong with that. After reading this you can name your own favourite food, say why you like it, and try one new food without worry.
item.title: My Favorite Foods
